earnings_release_evidence.claim: Management highlighted a Rule of 40 score of 145% and said full-year revenue guidance was raised due to confidence in an accelerating U.S. market.

filing_evidence.title: 10-Q
filing_evidence.claim: Palantir states that many customer contracts can be terminated for convenience with less than twelve months’ notice, limiting the certainty of multi-year contracted revenue conversion.
filing_evidence.summary: Contract termination-for-convenience clauses reduce certainty around backlog and long-term contract value realization.
filing_evidence.excerpt: The Company’s arrangements with its customers often have terms that span over multiple years. However, the Company allows many of its customers to terminate contracts for convenience prior to the end of the stated term with less than twelve months’ notice.
filing_evidence.notes: Numerical RPO values were not available in the provided text excerpt.

filing_evidence.title: 10-Q
filing_evidence.claim: Palantir’s disclosed remaining performance obligations exclude cancelable contracted revenue, including customer deposits, and also exclude contracts with original terms of twelve months or less under a practical expedient.
filing_evidence.summary: RPO disclosure represents noncancelable revenue and does not capture all contractual activity.
filing_evidence.excerpt: Revenue allocated to remaining performance obligations represents noncancelable contracted revenue that has not yet been recognized, which includes deferred revenue and, in certain instances, amounts that will be invoiced. The Company has elected the practical expedient allowing the Company to not disclose remaining performance obligations for contracts with original terms of twelve months or less. Cancelable contracted revenue, which includes customer deposits, is not considered a remaining performance obligation.
filing_evidence.notes: This affects interpretation of RPO/backlog metrics; provided 10-Q text did not include readable RPO amounts.
